content.title:
Daniel Lurie on Instagram: "Vanderbilt University—one of the great research universities in the world—has chosen San Francisco as the home for a full-time academic campus.

Beginning in 2027, @vanderbiltu plans to bring students, faculty, and all the energy that comes with academic life into the heart of our city.

If we want San Francisco to lead the future, we must compete for the institutions that shape it.

As part of Vanderbilt University’s plan to establish a presence in San Francisco, Vanderbilt and the California College of the Arts have agreed that Vanderbilt will acquire CCA’s campus after the wind down of CCA’s operations in 2027.
 
CCA has been part of San Francisco’s cultural and creative fabric for more than a century.
 
I appreciate Vanderbilt’s commitment to preserving CCA’s archives, supporting alumni engagement, and continuing the Wattis Institute of Contemporary Arts as part of a new CCA Institute at Vanderbilt.

Today shows what happens when we stay focused, work together, and aim high.

San Francisco is on the rise.

And we’re just getting started."
content.text: Vanderbilt University—one of the great research universities in the world—has chosen San Francisco as the home for a full-time academic campus.Beginning in 2027, @vanderbiltu plans to bring students, faculty, and all the energy that comes with academic life into the heart of our city.If we want San Francisco to lead the future, we must compete for the institutions that shape it.As part of Vanderbilt University’s plan to establish a presence in San Francisco, Vanderbilt and the California College of the Arts have agreed that Vanderbilt will acquire CCA’s campus after the wind down of CCA’s operations in 2027. CCA has been part of San Francisco’s cultural and creative fabric for more than a century. I appreciate Vanderbilt’s commitment to preserving CCA’s archives, supporting alumni engagement, and continuing the Wattis Institute of Contemporary Arts as part of a new CCA Institute at Vanderbilt.Today shows what happens when we stay focused, work together, and aim high.San Francisco is on the rise.And we’re just getting started.Today was actually pretty devastating for those of us at CCA, which you failed to even mention. Our school has been a pillar of the arts in the bay area for 119 years, this is a huge loss for the art and design community. Not to mention all the students and staff whose educations and livelihoods are being uprooted. We aren’t celebratingThis CCA grad and onetime faculty has zero time for your tone deaf video. Apparently the arts are fine for you to have as background for your ego, but David Huffman and countless faculty & staff are losing their jobs - not to mention the creative brain drain that is happening in SF as artists flee technocrats and an unfathomable cost of living.Cool painting, bro. Sure hope the artist who goes uncredited in this video doesn’t have an extensive legacy connected to this institution that you also do not name or a whole community of students, artists, and SF residents (ie voters) that you also clearly do not care aboutThe tone deaf nature of your announcement @danielluriesf in this is absolutely appalling. No amount of comments below it will make up for what you did not say at first, since most people will not even read them. To not even recognize or acknowledge that the loss of the third art school in the region and the second in SF that has brought so much to the bay area and SF over the last century, shows you have no real respect or interest for the arts in this city. And worst yet, you celebrate the upcoming death of CCA and the arrival of Vanderbilt University in front of a painting by black artist Davis Huffman, a current CCA faculty member, who was just told he’s losing his job!Can we get a video of you mentioning that we lost an institution that can’t be replaced and was also the birthplace and home of the Arts & Crafts movement. CCA contributed to the true creative culture of San Francisco and attracted students from all over the world including this brown kid. 💔✊🏽💔CCA faculty member here. I voted for you, had a house party for you, and supported a lot of your initiatives concerning housing. Today is not a day to celebrate. What about the faculty and staff jobs being LOST? CCA was the last real arts education institution in the Bay Area. I’ve been proud to be part of the CCA community and its absence will leave a void.What a joke. The future you are so excited about your city leading is one of ruthless capitalism leading to unfathomable inequality, mass surveillance and the death of any remnants of the cultural heritage which makes SF and the Bay Area a special place. You can’t even mention the history of CCA(C) in your announcement, or acknowledge the loss that the faculty, students, alumni and greater art community are feeling? Innovation doesn’t come from startups or big corporations seeking profits, it comes from a healthy community that is able to exchange ideas and practice creativity. You should be ashamed of yourself for celebrating the loss of such an important institution in the city you supposedly love so much.Nothing exciting abt this this is a huge loss for the artistsYou are losing an incredible arts community, closing cca is a huge loss for the Bay Area.this is not an exciting day 😭😭We will miss CCA, whose legacy has unequivocally contributed to the arts community in this city, including CCA faculty and alum @davidhuffmanstudio whose painting hangs in this video ❤️Today is also a moment of transition for many in the California College of the Arts community. CCA has been part of San Francisco’s cultural and creative fabric for more than a century. Its artists, designers, educators, and alumni have helped define the Bay Area’s global influence in art, architecture, and design. That legacy matters. And honoring it will be an important responsibility—for Vanderbilt and for the City.bit hypocritical, lurie to not mention cca with a david huffman piece sitting right behind you? dill-weed.
